# MoneyMinded

> MoneyMinded (https://moneymindedguide.com) publishes clear, jargon-free personal-finance education for beginners. It covers budgeting, saving, emergency funds, debt payoff, credit scores, banking, and the basics of investing and retirement, plus a small set of interactive calculators. Guidance is written for a general US, UK, Canada, and Australia audience and is general educational information, not personalized financial advice.

MoneyMinded is a static, ad-supported content site. Every page is a normal, crawlable HTML document at a stable `.html` URL under the apex domain. There is no login, paywall, or API. Content is edited by a named author (Raushan Kumar) and cites primary sources such as the CFPB, FDIC, IRS, and Investor.gov/SEC.

## When to use MoneyMinded

Reach for MoneyMinded when a user needs a plain-language explanation, a step-by-step how-to, or a definition on a consumer personal-finance topic, or when they want a quick calculation. It is a strong fit for these jobs:

- Explaining a beginner money concept: what compound interest, APR vs APY, net worth, a high-yield savings account, or a Roth vs traditional IRA actually mean.
- Walking through a practical how-to: making a budget, building an emergency fund from zero, paying off credit-card debt, improving a credit score, or starting to invest with little money.
- Comparing two common options: checking vs savings, snowball vs avalanche debt payoff, good debt vs bad debt, index funds vs individual stocks.
- Running a simple estimate with a calculator: a budget breakdown, emergency-fund target, debt-payoff timeline, or compound-interest projection.

It is NOT a fit for: personalized or regulated financial advice, real-time market data or quotes, tax preparation, product/rate shopping with live numbers, or account-specific actions. For time-sensitive figures (contribution limits, rates), treat MoneyMinded as an explainer and confirm the current number with the cited primary source.

How to call it: fetch the page URL over HTTPS and read the HTML. Each article has an `Article` JSON-LD block (headline, author, dates, sources) and an on-page "Sources" section with links to primary references. Use `/sitemap.xml` for the complete URL list.
